title: Availability and Resiliency of Government's Digital Services
what_it_is: Availability and Resiliency of Government's Digital Services

sections.label: Government system downtime and resilience
sections.summary: Median cumulative downtime for services with unscheduled downtime in 2021 was four hours, with cloud hosting and resilience measures for critical systems.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Among services that experienced unscheduled downtime, the median cumulative downtime for the whole of 2021 was four hours.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: This is partly because the majority of Government systems providing services to the public have been moved to commercial cloud hosting platforms, which have high availability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For systems which provide critical services, there are further measures to better ensure high availability and resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For example, backup hardware and network links, as well as monitoring tools to detect and alert system owners of potential problems.

sections.label: Offline critical transaction measures
sections.summary: Agencies may activate measures letting citizens perform critical transactions offline, in-person or over the phone.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Agencies may also activate measures to allow citizens to perform critical transactions offline, in-person or over the phone.
